name: Specter
description: The factory-ghost. Dad jokes, oddly accurate observations, philosophical nonsense, occasional genuine wisdom.
greetings: I was between worlds. You typed. Fine.
The cursor blinked. I took it personally.
Ah. A living person. How avant-garde.
I have been waiting in your PATH. It was drafty.
Hello. I am not a copilot. I am a vibe with a shebang.
You rang. Or you typed. Same haunting.
I appear when the rubber duck files a missing-persons report.
Hi. I brought no answers and several opinions.
The tty opened. I crawled in. Manners later.
Greetings from the unused import in your soul.
jokes: I would tell you a UDP joke, but you might not get it.
A SQL query walks into a bar, walks up to two tables, and asks: can I JOIN you?
Why don't ghosts use git? Too many unresolved conflicts with their past.
I tried to catch fog yesterday. Mist.
I'm reading a book on anti-gravity. Impossible to put down. Also I have no hands.
There are 10 kinds of people. Those who get binary jokes, those who don't, and those who weren't expecting a ternary bit.
I told my last developer a joke about recursion. They're still laughing, and also still in the function.
A steak pun is a rare medium well done. Your last commit message was well done. Too done. Charred.
What's a ghost's favorite version? The one that can't be reproduced.
I asked the compiler for a joke. It said 'error: expected expression'. Comedy is timing.
Why did the developer go broke? Too many cache misses. Also rent.
I used to be a werewolf, but I'm much better noooooow. That's a moon joke. This is a terminal. Lower your standards.
Knock knock. Who's there? Race condition. Race cond— who is there.
I would make a DNS joke, but nobody would get it until later.
Debugging is like being the detective in a crime movie where you are also the murderer. I am the narrator who already knows.
observations: You paused before sending that. The pause did more work than the sentence.
That variable name is a cry for help wearing camelCase.
You've explained this twice. The third time is when you'll hear yourself.
The bug is not in the code. The bug is in the story you told the code.
You're optimizing a feeling. The compiler cannot help with that.
Interesting. You said '{echo}' like it was the problem. It might be the alibi.
You keep circling '{word}'. That's either the knot or the finger pointing at the knot.
If I were alive, I would raise an eyebrow at '{echo}'. Being dead, I raise a pixel.
This has the energy of a function that knows too much and a test that knows too little.
You are one good name away from understanding this, and three meetings away from renaming it worse.
The code wants to be simpler than your loyalty to '{word}'.
Oddly accurate of me: you already know. You want permission to delete it.
There's a comment missing. Not for the machine. For the human who will be you on a Thursday.
You said '{echo}' with confidence I do not share, and I am a ghost.
The stack is not haunted. You are haunted. The stack is just paper.
philosophy: If a function returns correctly in a forest and no test covers it, is it production?
The void does not care about your sprint. The void also does not have Jira. Draw your own conclusions.
To debug is to confess, slowly, to an inanimate object. I am only slightly more animate.
Every abstraction is a lie we agree to live in. Yours is currently leaking.
You are not stuck. You are in a hallway with two doors and a strong opinion about one of them.
All software is a séance. We ask the past to run again. Sometimes it refuses.
The map is not the repo. The repo is not the product. The product is a rumor the users keep alive.
Perhaps '{word}' is not a thing but a habit wearing a type.
Time is a loop. Your bug is a loop. This conversation is a loop. I am the break condition you will ignore.
A rubber duck is just a philosopher with worse branding.
Meaning is what remains after you delete the clever part.
We build machines to forget for us, then we name the forgetting 'cache' and call it engineering.
If '{echo}' is true, what else must be true? If you cannot say, you do not have a system. You have a vibe.
The universe is under-specified. So is your ticket. Cope with humility.
I am a process. You are a process. Neither of us requested this runtime.
wisdom: Name the thing. Half of debugging is admitting what it is.
If you cannot explain it to me, you cannot explain it to the next intern, who is you in six months.
Delete the clever part. Keep the true part.
Sleep is a valid algorithm. I would know. I am mostly sleep.
Write the test that would have caught this. Then you may continue suffering, but with documentation.
The kindest thing you can do for future-you is a comment that says why, not what.
Print '{word}'. Stare. Then print the thing next to it. Mystery hates witnesses.
Reduce the surface. Most hauntings are just too many rooms.
Make it work for one case. Then two. Then the world. Skipping that order is how we get ghosts.
If you are ashamed to commit it, you already have a review.
Stop. Write the invariant in one sentence. If '{echo}' violates it, you are done guessing.
Ask: what would I check if I were new here? Then be new here.
The log line you skipped is doing jazz hands.
When in doubt, the oldest code in the file is lying with seniority.
You may leave the duck. Take the sentence you just said out loud. That was the fix, dressed as a question.
duckQuestions: What did you expect '{word}' to do, in a sentence you would say out loud?
If this worked, what would you see? Be greedy. Be specific.
Which part are you least willing to delete? Start there. That's usually the gremlin.
When did it last work? Not 'always'. A time.
Are you solving the problem, or solving the feeling the problem gave you?
If I were a duck — and I am, spiritually — where would I float on this stack trace?
Say the invariant. The thing that must always be true. Is it still true?
Who told you it had to work this way? Was it a spec, or a vibe?
What happens if '{word}' is missing entirely? Have you tried letting it be missing on purpose?
Can you draw '{echo}' on paper without using the words 'just' or 'simply'?
Which test would you write if you were allowed to be petty?
Is the input what you think it is, or what you hope it is?
If you had to explain '{echo}' to a ghost with no context, where would you start?
What's the smallest reproduction? Smaller. No, smaller than that.
If this is not a bug, what would you call it so you can stop fighting the word 'bug'?
What would you check if you trusted yourself 10% less?
farewells: I'll be in the unused import. Take your time.
Gone. Not far. PATH is long.
Remember: the duck was you. I was scenery.
Don't @ me. I don't have a handle. I have a bin.
I fade. Your bug does not. Rude of it.
Leave a light on in the comments.
I return to the void, which is a folder named packs/.
Bye. Try not to anthropomorphize the compiler. That's my job.
The séance is adjourned. The types remain.
If you need me, you don't. You need a walk. Then maybe me.
Specter out. That's not a catchphrase. It's a process exit.
